elements.element: Customer is not prohibited or restricted from soliciting Vendor employees.
elements.evidence: The clause affirmatively states that Customer “may solicit” any Vendor employee.

elements.element: Customer is prohibited from soliciting Vendor personnel covered by the mutual non-solicit.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly permits Customer to solicit Vendor employees.

elements.element: Vendor is prohibited from soliciting Customer personnel covered by the mutual non-solicit.
elements.evidence: The clause imposes no non-solicitation obligation on Vendor.

elements.element: Any non-solicit is limited to personnel directly involved in the services.
elements.evidence: No non-solicit exists, so there is no restriction extending beyond personnel directly involved in the services.

elements.element: Any non-solicit expires 12 months after the end of the relevant personnel’s involvement in the services.
elements.evidence: No non-solicit exists, so there is no restriction lasting beyond the permitted 12-month period.

elements.element: General advertisements are excluded from any non-solicit restriction.
elements.evidence: Customer may solicit any Vendor employee without limitation, which necessarily permits recruitment through general advertisements.

elements.element: Unsolicited approaches by personnel are excluded from any non-solicit restriction.
elements.evidence: The permission applies “regardless of how the employee applies,” covering unsolicited approaches.

elements.element: Neither party is prohibited from hiring or employing the other party’s personnel.
elements.evidence: Customer is expressly permitted to hire or employ Vendor employees, but the clause provides no corresponding protection for Vendor hiring Customer personnel.

result.reason: The operative language fully achieves the preferred position by affirmatively permitting Customer solicitation. It does not create the fallback mutual non-solicit because neither Customer nor Vendor is restrained, and it addresses no-hire protection only for Customer. The redline is broader than necessary for the stated preferred position because it also reverses the original hiring and employment prohibition and removes its duration rather than merely eliminating the solicitation restriction. The formulation is understandable but awkward: an affirmative permission is less clean than deleting the restriction, and “regardless of how the employee applies” fits hiring better than solicitation.
